name: Genetic Facial Cleft

ethnicAssociations: varies by population, higher in some Asian and Native American groups

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Genetic Facial Cleft

criteria.description: Presence of a congenital facial cleft involving lip, alveolus, and/or palate
Positive family history of facial clefts or related craniofacial anomalies
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with craniofacial development
Presence of additional craniofacial or systemic anomalies consistent with syndromic forms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital facial cleft plus either positive family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may require multidisciplinary evaluation including genetics, otolaryngology, and craniofacial surgery.

searchTerms: lip gap on one or both sides

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cleft palate involving the secondary palate
searchTerms: split in the roof of mouth

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to oronasal communication
searchTerms: difficulty eating due to palate opening

occasional.symptomName: Hearing impairment secondary to Eustachian tube dysfunction
searchTerms: hearing loss from ear tube problems
Eustachian tube dysfunction causing hearing issues

occasional.symptomName: Psychosocial difficulties related to facial appearance
searchTerms: psychological issues related to face look
emotional problems due to facial differences

rare.symptomName: Cleft-related airway anomalies requiring surgical intervention
searchTerms: airway problems from cleft needing surgery
breathing issues due to palate defect

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying mutations in IRF6, MSX1, or other craniofacial development genes
imaging: 3D craniofacial CT scan demonstrating extent of bony clefts
MRI to assess associated soft tissue and brain anomalies
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as IRF6, TP63, MSX1, and FGFR1
other: Clinical examination revealing cleft lip and/or palate
Audiologic evaluation for middle ear function

distinguishingFeatures: Autosomal dominant inheritance with variable expressivity
Respiratory distress due to airway obstruction

redFlags: Respiratory distress due to airway obstruction
Failure to thrive secondary to feeding difficulties
Recurrent otitis media with hearing loss
